artists.biography: Tim Bowness is a british singer/songwriter primarily known for his work as part of the band No-Man, a long-term project with Steven Wilson from Porcupine Tree.  In addition to producing several albums with No-Man, Tim has recorded with popular Italian artist Alice, experimental guitar legend David Torn, Soft Machine's Hugh Hopper, Roger Eno, German band Centrozoon, and recorded the album Flame (1994) in collaboration with Porcupine Tree/ex-Japan keyboard player Richard Barbieri.  Tim's debut solo album, My Hotel Year, was released on the One Little Indian label in 2004.

Tim Bowness.biography: Tim Bowness is a british singer/songwriter primarily known for his work as part of the band No-Man, a long-term project with Steven Wilson from Porcupine Tree.  In addition to producing several albums with No-Man, Tim has recorded with popular Italian artist Alice, experimental guitar legend David Torn, Soft Machine's Hugh Hopper, Roger Eno, German band Centrozoon, and recorded the album Flame (1994) in collaboration with Porcupine Tree/ex-Japan keyboard player Richard Barbieri.  Tim's debut solo album, My Hotel Year, was released on the One Little Indian label in 2004.

perplexity.description:
Released on February 17, 2017, through InsideOut Music, Lost In The Ghost Light is the fourth solo album by Tim Bowness, best known as the vocalist and co-writer of No-Man. The album is a concept work centered around the fictional character Jeff Harrison, a progressive rock musician reflecting on his career and the music industry. Musically, it blends lush, atmospheric rock with elements of art rock and progressive pop, drawing inspiration from the classic sounds of 1970s progressive rock. The arrangements are rich and layered, featuring contributions from notable musicians such as Steven Wilson (who also mixed and mastered the album), Bruce Soord, Colin Edwin, and guests including Ian Anderson and Kit Watkins.

Lost In The Ghost Light stands as a pivotal release in Bowness’s solo discography, marking a shift toward a more expansive and narrative-driven approach. It follows his acclaimed 2015 album Stupid Things That Mean the World, but distinguishes itself with a deeper conceptual focus and a more overt homage to the progressive rock genre. The album received widespread critical acclaim for its emotional depth, sophisticated songwriting, and evocative production, with reviewers highlighting its elegiac tone and musical richness. It was widely regarded as one of the standout progressive rock releases of 2017, cementing Bowness’s reputation as a leading voice in contemporary art rock.
